subject: Unit economics deep-dive / follow-up: inference cost, $/1M tokens, CAC payback

Subject: Unit economics deep-dive — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap + agreed next steps so we have alignment before the follow-up deep-dive.

Call highlights
- High-level use case: realtime underwriting assistant + batch statement summarization for customer support.
- Expected traffic profile (est): 8M–12M tokens/month year 1, ramp to 25M–40M tokens/month by Q4 if conversion tests succeed.
- Target business metric: keep incremental inference cost under $X per feature (see details below) and aim for overall feature margin >40% after inference.

Open questions we agreed to validate in the deep-dive:
1) Precise tokenization assumptions per feature (avg tokens per request for scoring vs summarization).
2) Acceptable latency targets for the realtime flow (SLO 150ms p95 preferred).
3) Budget range for hosted inference vs dedicated capacity (you mentioned a target spend band of $10k–$25k/mo initially).

Next steps
- I’ll send a short unit-economics model with a couple pricing scenarios ($/1M tokens) and example $/feature calculations. (Attached: unit_econ_modeling.xlsx)
- Dev will run a quick latency/cost sketch for both Hosted API and Dedicated (rough ballpark) and share recommended config.
- Samir/Alicia: if you can share a few sample prompts or average character lengths per request, we’ll lock tokens-per-call assumptions.

Attachment stubs: unit_econ_modeling.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-pricing-options.pdf (pricing summary).

Thanks — aiming to have the model + initial config to you by Friday.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Unit economics deep-dive — post-call recap & next steps

Appreciate the recap — that lines up with what we discussed. A couple clarifications before you finalize the model:

1) Tokens per feature: for the underwriting assistant we’re seeing roughly 250–400 tokens per request (prompt + expected response), and for statement summarization ~1,200 tokens per document on average. We’ll send a small sample set later today.
2) Budget: the $10k–$25k/mo was a preliminary internal band; leadership is flexible but wants to see clear $/1M token scenarios and how that maps to CAC payback and margin. If you can show a target $/1M token that gets us to >40% contribution margin on the feature, that’ll help.
3) CAC payback: our sales motion averages 4–6 months; we need to understand required ARPU per customer to hit payback under 6 months given inference cost per active user.

Also, can you provide example $/feature tees (e.g., inference cost per active user per month at 10k DAU, 30k DAU) so we can map to finance. Thanks — Samir

—Samir

Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unit economics deep-dive — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Samir — answering inline and attaching the worked model.

> Tokens per feature
- Using your ranges, I modeled: underwriting assistant avg 325 tokens/call, summarization 1,200 tokens/doc.

> Target $/1M tokens and margin
- Scenario A (Hosted, standard models + optimistic batching): $40 / 1M tokens -> inference cost to you (net) after our committed discounts ~ $32 / 1M.
- Scenario B (Dedicated + quantized model): $18 / 1M tokens -> inference cost to you (net) after committed reserved capacity ~ $14 / 1M.
- In the workbook I show per-feature math: e.g., underwriting: 325 tokens * 1M tokens bucket -> ~3,076 requests per 1M tokens; cost per request (Scenario A) ~$0.013, (Scenario B) ~$0.0045.

> $/feature examples (monthly active users basis)
- Example: 10k DAU (active users) with 2 underwriting requests/day average -> monthly requests = 10k * 2 * 30 = 600k requests -> tokens = 600k * 325 = 195M tokens/month.
  - Scenario A inference cost = 195 * $40 = $7,800/month (note: $40 per 1M -> multiply by 195).
  - Scenario B inference cost = 195 * $18 = $3,510/month.
  - Per-active-user inference cost/month: Scenario A ~$0.78, Scenario B ~$0.35.

> CAC payback calc (simple)
- Assume ARPU per paying customer $30/mo, gross margin target pre-inference 70%. Contribution margin after inference = 70% - (inference cost / ARPU). Using Scenario B per-user inference cost $0.35, contribution ~= 70% - (0.35/30) ~ 68.8% -> payback primarily driven by CAC itself.
- If you need payback <6 months, show us CAC and conversion rates and we’ll compute exact thresholds; the workbook includes a calculator tab for that.

> Margin targets vs inference cost
- Typical target: keep inference as <5% of ARPU for high-margin features; up to 10% for strategic/engagement features where accuracy matters.
- Using your ARPU $30 target, 5% -> $1.50/month allowed for inference per active user. That corresponds to ~430M tokens/month at Scenario B pricing per 10k DAU with current usage patterns (see sheet).

Attachments included: unit_econ_modeling.xlsx (workbook with scenarios, per-feature tabs), redwood-pricing-options.pdf (detail on Hosted vs Dedicated assumptions).

We’ll also include two config sketches (Dev) for latency vs cost tradeoffs: Hosted with aggressive batching vs Dedicated with lower quantization. Aditya/Dev — can you add any notes on expected p95 latency for the configs?

If this looks sensible I can package a short one-pager for leadership with the core $/1M scenarios and the DAU/$/feature examples.

Thanks — sending the workbook link now.

—Marissa
